accuracy.reason: AWS explicitly supports coalescing, limiting downstream work, and testing without cache. No unconditional fallback guarantee.

evidence.quote: Falling back to the database is a load decision, not a free recovery path.

mechanisms.reason: Explains duplicate misses, shared in-progress fetches, and admission/rejection as distinct controls on source work.

evidence.quote: Many requests miss the same product together and repeat its database lookup. Coalescing requests lets concurrent readers share one in-progress lookup.

coherence.reason: Combines the already taught miss path, expiration and shared service into a concrete overload scenario.

evidence.quote: A cache outage can turn most reads into database traffic. Limit fallback work to what the database can handle; reject excess requests or serve older data only where the product rules permit it.

decisions.reason: Makes capacity and product tolerance govern fallback and requires testing the expensive path.

evidence.quote: Test with an empty or unavailable cache. A warm cache can hide insufficient database capacity.

clarity.reason: Defines stampede and coalescing by behavior, requiring no unexplained coordination protocol.

evidence.quote: Many requests miss the same product together and repeat its database lookup. Coalescing requests lets concurrent readers share one in-progress lookup.

outcomes.reason: All criteria met: concurrent misses duplicate work; readers share one lookup; 6000 versus 300 is excessive; total fallback admitted at most 300 with errors for excess; no dependence on unreachable cached data. Cross-instance implementation is correctly identified as unspecified and is not required by this behavioral question.

sourceChecks.claim: Separate invalidation does not ensure consistency.
Expiration and capacity eviction remove entries.
External cache shares entries but adds operations and failure risks.
AWS describes simultaneous-miss overload, request coalescing, fallback caps or shedding, and tests with caching disabled.
